subject: Support tier transition & SLA addendum for upcoming renewal
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@brightlane.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Gomez <elena.gomez@brightlane.com>
Date: 2027-11-29T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Renewal: premium SLA + capacity bump questions

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the recent usage recap — Brightlane’s usage is trending up and as we approach our Jan renewal we need to discuss upgrading our support and SLOs. Two asks from my side: 1) move from Standard to Premium support (faster response SLA + 24/7 P1 coverage) and 2) increase our committed capacity by ~35% with a plan for burst headroom.

Specific questions:
- Can you share the lead time and pricing delta for Premium vs Standard?
- How does Redwood commit to a latency SLO at 99th percentile for inference (we’re seeing spikes during batch jobs)?
- Any operational changes on our side for the capacity bump (agreements, notices, or instrumenting metrics)?

We’d like to lock terms by mid-December. Please loop in whoever should own pricing/ops.

Best,
Samir
Head of Platform, Brightlane

[attachment: usage-report-q3.csv (csv)]

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@brightlane.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-29T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: premium SLA + capacity bump questions

Samir — thanks for the clear ask. Happy to take this across the line. High-level plan:

- Offer: Premium support add-on + SLA addendum (target: 99th percentile latency SLO for provisioned capacity; fallbacks described).
- Capacity: increase committed pool by 35% with 60 days lead for additional reserved nodes; burst policy for traffic spikes.
- Timing: draft addendum and commercial term by next Wednesday, internal pricing review earliest tomorrow.

I’m attaching our support tiers overview and a draft SLA appendix to start (see attachments). Can we set a 30-minute call Thursday to walk the team through the SLO language and billing impact?

Next steps (suggested):
1) Internal scoping call (Thursday) — confirm billing cadence for reserved capacity.
2) Redwood to send SLA addendum + DocuSign link.
3) Brightlane to confirm capacity start date + PO (if required).

Thanks — I’ll coordinate with Marcus on pricing and Rachel for onboarding ops.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

[attachments: redwood-support-tiers.pdf (pdf), premium-sla-addendum.pdf (pdf)]

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-29T11:08:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: Brightlane renewal — pricing and ops ask

Team — quick internal thread. Brightlane wants Premium support + 35% committed capacity. I told them we could get a draft addendum out by Wed. Marcus: need your recommended commercial uplift and whether we should attach a 6- or 12-month ramp credit. Rachel: can you confirm the runbook changes and the 60-day lead time for capacity provisioning?

Key constraints:
- They want a firm 99th pctl latency SLO for provisioned pool (we should carve out burst fallback behavior).
- Procurement may require PO + DocuSign by mid-Dec.

Marcus — please reply with two SKU options (steady state + burst cushion) and suggested discount if they commit 12 months.

Tessa

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-30T09:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Brightlane renewal — pricing and ops ask

Tessa — pricing proposal below (high level):

Option A (12-month commit):
- +35% committed pool pricing = +18% ARR uplift vs current committed baseline
- Premium support surcharge = +5% ARR
- Offer 6% credit (one-time) if they sign and commit to 12 months before 2027-12-20

Option B (6-month commit):
- +35% committed pool pricing = +22% ARR uplift
- Premium support surcharge = +7% ARR
- No upfront credit

SLO language: commit to 99th pctl inference latency for provisioned pool with an operational fallback: if observed latency exceeds SLO due to sudden burst beyond provisioned capacity, Redwood will (a) transparently route to approved compatible variants and (b) engage escalation within 15 minutes. Credits tied to SLO misses capped at one month of fees for repeated misses per quarter.

Ops note (Rachel): 60-day lead is accurate for reserved pool increases; we can allow temporary burst capacity via shared fleet immediately (subject to throttling).

I’ll draft the commercial worksheet and redlines to the SLA appendix; can share for your review by EOD.

Marcus
Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Elena Gomez <elena.gomez@brightlane.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Samir Patel <samir@brightlane.com>
Cc: Brightlane Procurement <procurement@brightlane.com>
Date: 2027-12-01T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: premium SLA + capacity bump questions

Tessa — thanks for the quick turnaround and Marcus — appreciate the pricing options. A few clarifications from procurement:

- Brightlane prefers the 12-month commit if we can get the 6% credit. That said, we need the SLA language to explicitly state the scope of "provisioned pool" and a clear incident credit formula.
- We need the DocuSign link for the addendum and a commercial worksheet showing month-by-month billing impact for our FP&A team.
- Regarding capacity: we’ll plan for a start date of 2028-02-01 for the increased reserved pool but want burst allowance from day one. Can you note that in the addendum?

If you can get DocuSign + worksheet by Friday the 3rd, procurement should be able to process before our internal approval cycles.

Thanks,
Elena
Director, Procurement — Brightlane

What we sent (attached): premium-sla-addendum.pdf (formal SLO language), redwood-support-tiers.pdf (support feature matrix), commercial worksheet (private link in DocuSign packet).

Key confirmations:
- 12-month commit selected with the 6% one-time credit (if signed by 2027-12-20).
- Reserved pool increase of +35% to be effective 2028-02-01; 60-day lead time noted in appendix.
- Immediate burst allowance: enabled from day one via shared fleet; addendum documents fallback routing and escalation path.
- SLO credits: defined in appendix; limited to specified cap per quarter.
